I’m 48 this year, and I’ve farmed here in Quzhou for a long time. I only went to middle school, so I don’t sit and calculate like a technician, but I do watch my fields, remember what happened in past years, and compare with what other farmers nearby are doing. This year I’ll still keep cotton as the main crop, because on my 12 mu that’s the safer cash crop for me, and my family has off-farm work so I can’t spread labor too thin. But I won’t put all the land into cotton. I’ll keep 4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. That way I have some grain coming in and I’m not depending on one crop only.

For cotton, I’ll put 8 mu. Cotton needs more labor, especially later for pest watching and picking, but with well water I can still manage it. I’ll use improved seed, not the most expensive one, just the variety people around here have been using steadily. Fertilizer, I’ll do a base application and then one topdress, not too low because cotton without enough fertilizer gives weak plants, but not too high either because fertilizer is not cheap and too much can make the crop too lush. For the 4 mu wheat-maize land, I’ll handle it more in the usual local way. Wheat goes in early October, gets base fertilizer, then one topdress at jointing, with 2 irrigations if spring is dry. After wheat harvest in June, maize has to go in fast. The turnaround is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly. Maize I’ll fertilize once at planting and once around the big bell stage if it looks like it needs pushing. This plan is not about chasing the highest yield. It’s about keeping costs under control, matching my family labor, and making sure I still get a decent harvest even if the season is only average.
